body.title: Per-family model definitions served by the daemon
body.intent: Introduce daemon-owned built-in definitions for Claude CLI, Codex CLI, and Ollama, exposed through IPC to the TUI, VS Code plugin, and JetBrains plugin, with migration delivered in stages. Consolidate runner identity, CLI kind, tier defaults, summariser fallback, reasoning-effort transport and accepted levels, input-size limits, structured-output quirks, and model-id rules. Support model-specific tier and effort mappings, user-selected models, and capability overrides. The model-level facts (model ids, tier defaults, summariser model, per-model effort levels and input limits) live in a data file shipped in the repo, not in code and not in the user's config.json, so a model or version update needs no code change [c2].
body.scopeBoundary: Covers the three built-in families only; the families and their transport and structured-output handling stay in code, while models are configured through the repo-shipped data file [c2]. The daemon is the single authority: the TUI and both IDE plugins read definitions over IPC and keep no copy. Every hardcoded runner/model string is migrated, in stages. Require an explicit capability profile for any selected model absent from the built-in definitions: insrc probes the model through its CLI for each claimed effort level (plus `codex debug models` for codex), shows the results, and the user approves or rejects the model [c3].
nonGoals: User-defined model families or runner implementations.
All consumers in one coordinated release
Use conservative family defaults plus overrides
Inherit the family's default model profile

ruledOut: All consumers in one coordinated release
decisions.reason: The idea identifies duplicated facts across four consumers, but does not yet establish whether the plugins are part of this effort or how their migrations should be coordinated.
All consumers are already in scope for staged migration. Settling extensibility determines whether their shared contract is a consolidated catalog or a configurable provider system.
Built-in families with configurable models is settled. This decision defines what configuring a model permits without reopening family extensibility or migration scope.

All four consumers are in scope, and configurable models with capability overrides are settled. Choosing the authority now determines how staged migrations keep capability displays and actual execution consistent.

ruledOut: Use conservative family defaults plus overrides
Inherit the family's default model profile
decisions.reason: Daemon-owned definitions and configurable models are settled. Model-specific differences mean that selecting an unfamiliar model still needs a defined capability policy.

citations.quotedText: models especially their version get updated quite frequently, requiring a code change would be very cumbersome. separate config file in the repo, not user's config.json that stores the model structure
test and approve or reject the unknown model
